title: Will using straps destroy your wrists?
summary: After a deadlift session NH debunks the claim that lifting straps injure the wrists. He points out that wrist loading happens in any pull, that he has used straps for a year with only minor bruising, and that strongmen pull and carry huge weights with straps without wrist injuries. He argues straps actually reduce injury risk and that anti-strap dogma costs people gains.

claims.claim: Many YouTube fitness voices, usually minimalists and often powerlifters, are anti-straps, and 99% of their arguments are demonstrably false.
Common anti-strap claims include that straps ruin form, impair growth, cause injuries, or turn the deadlift into a different lift that loses its benefits; he finds these silly.
The idea that straps strain wrist tendons is never applied to other pulls, even though every deadlift grip or weighted pull-up also loads the wrist.
Straps reduce injury risk because you avoid the mixed grip and don't need the hook grip.
He has used straps for a year with submaximal weights; the only effect is marks or bruising on the wrist, never pain, and a bruise is not an injury.

Strongmen pull around a thousand pounds with straps from the floor or blocks and do farmer's walks and frame carries with around 800 lbs in straps, yet he has never heard of one injuring a wrist from straps.
People also wrongly tie straps to ego to discourage using them for rows and upper back work; avoiding straps out of fear means missing out on gains because straps are amazing.
Dogmatism has no place in lifting; it only damages the progress of people who want to get bigger and better.

cues: no need for mixed or hook grip
